blocks.text: Chilliwack Condos Under $800K: Practical and Spacious

parts.t: Chilliwack condos under $800K provide exceptional Fraser Valley value with modern amenities, mountain views, and the outdoor lifestyle at accessible pricing. These properties attract first-time buyers, young professionals, and downsizers seeking quality living without single-family home maintenance or costs.

The market includes options from cozy one-bedroom units to spacious two and three-bedroom family condos, many in newer buildings with contemporary designs and amenities. Residents appreciate Chilliwack's natural beauty with hiking and water sports minutes away, improving downtown with local restaurants and shops, plus the genuine small-town atmosphere. Many buildings offer fitness centres, social rooms, and well-maintained grounds enhancing community living. The area's affordability compared to Metro Vancouver combined with reasonable Highway 1 commuting makes Chilliwack increasingly popular. Excellent schools and recreation facilities serve families well, while the relaxed pace appeals to all ages. Ready to explore Chilliwack condos? blocks.text: Chilliwack Condos Under $800K Real Estate FAQs

parts.t: What can you buy for under $800,000 in the Chilliwack condo market?

Under $800,000 encompasses almost every apartment condo in Chilliwack, including older 1- and 2-bedroom low-rise units in Chilliwack Proper and Downtown ($280K–$430K), mid-age Sardis condos along Vedder Road and Luckakuck Way ($375K–$500K), and newer 2-bedroom-plus-den or top-floor suites in Garrison Crossing, Vedder Crossing, and District 1881 ($460K–$725K).
Which Chilliwack neighbourhoods have the most condo buildings?

Most condo buildings are located in Downtown Chilliwack and Chilliwack Proper (along Yale Road, Young Road, First Avenue, and Williams Street) and in Sardis / Garrison Crossing / Vedder Crossing (along Vedder Road, Garrison Boulevard, Market Way, and Promontory Road).
Are there 55+ age-restricted condo buildings in Chilliwack and Sardis?

Yes. While BC removed most rental and 19+/45+ strata age restrictions in 2022, 55+ age bylaws remain legally enforceable. Both Sardis (near Vedder Road and Luckakuck Way) and Chilliwack Proper have dedicated 55+ apartment buildings that often trade at a lower price per square foot than all-age buildings.
What do monthly strata fees typically cover in a Chilliwack condo?

Monthly strata fees in Chilliwack low-rise wood-frame buildings usually cover building insurance, exterior and roof maintenance, common-area landscaping, snow removal, garbage/recycling, management fees, and contingency reserve fund (CRF) contributions. Some older buildings also include hot water or natural gas for fireplaces.
Do Chilliwack condos under $800K qualify for the BC First-Time Home Buyers' PTT exemption?

Yes. Eligible first-time buyers purchasing a principal residence in BC receive a full Property Transfer Tax exemption up to a fair market value of $835,000 (with a partial exemption between $835,000 and $860,000), meaning every condo on this under-$800K page falls below the $835,000 full-exemption cap.
What strata documents should I review before buying a condo in Chilliwack?

Always review the Form B Information Certificate, the current Strata Bylaws, the most recent Depreciation Report, the building's Strata Insurance Summary (checking water damage deductibles), the Financial Statements, and at least 24 months of Strata Council, AGM, and SGM minutes.
Are there leasehold condos in the Chilliwack area?

Most condos in Sardis, Garrison Crossing, and Downtown Chilliwack are freehold strata (fee simple), whereas some developments on First Nations lands (such as along Vedder Road / Skowkale or Tzeachten lands) are prepaid residential leaseholds. Always verify whether a listing is freehold strata or leasehold before writing an offer.
